claims.claim_text: Milburn H. Stuckwish was chief engineer of WSOY in Decatur, Illinois, immediately before joining the Signal Corps in 1942, making WSOY his last documented civilian employer before military service.
claims.evidence_excerpt: chief engineer of WSOY, Decatur, Ill., has joined the Signal Corps
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A contemporary radio trade journal names Stuckwish, his WSOY role and the transition into Signal Corps service in one sentence.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the rare full name with middle initial, the protected-identifier Army bridge and the compatible mechanics-and-repair occupation category.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit immediate transition from WSOY to the Signal Corps in a June 1, 1942 report; the precise administrative dates still require the personnel file.
claims.match_notes: WSOY is a named employer. University of Illinois is described only as planned Signal Corps engineering training and is not classified as an employer.

claims.claim_text: The best-supported immediate pre-OSS pathway for Milburn H. Stuckwish is Signal Corps service after leaving WSOY; the OSS transfer date has not been located.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The June 1942 report places Signal Corps service immediately after WSOY employment and describes planned engineering training.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence person match; the protected identifier remains private.
claims.temporal_assessment: Probable immediate to OSS rather than explicit: the military transition is explicit, but no reviewed source dates the later OSS transfer.
claims.match_notes: Military assignment, not civilian employment. The personnel file remains necessary to resolve the 1942 report and 1943 Army-entry date.
